mathematical_boundaries: Ordinary potential perturbations and twisted Lee-compatible perturbations remain distinct. The Gauduchon volume problem fixes a Lee class and an identified twisted Bott–Chern class and concerns metric uniqueness, not uniqueness of a scalar modulo the kernel of the twisted operator. The Vaisman theorem requires a smooth positive volume invariant under both distinguished flows; its proof retains the competing metric’s scale until transverse integration fixes it. The rigidity theorem requires Gauduchon gauge and Chern–Ricci flatness for the same metric. Lee–Gauduchon duality tests only the image of the Lee map. The strongly Gauduchon mass estimate concerns closed positive currents and finite-dimensional de Rham norms, not a lower bound for nonlinear Monge–Ampère mass. The Calabi–Eckmann and balanced elliptic examples preserve both distinctions.
